prompt: Merge all the dependabot PRs in this repo please.
expected_output: The agent should check `gh auth status` and the repo's allowed merge methods, run scripts/dependabot_prs.py to inventory and classify the open Dependabot PRs, show the user a plan naming which PRs will be merged and which are skipped with reasons, then merge only minor/patch bumps with all checks green using `gh pr merge <n> --rebase --delete-branch`, one at a time, fast-forward the local base branch once the batch is merged, and finish with a summary of merged / skipped / failed.

prompt: clear out the dependabot backlog on hussainweb/skills — include the major bumps too, and squash them instead of rebasing
expected_output: The agent should scope work to the named repo via `--repo hussainweb/skills`, drop the minor-only version filter, keep the all-checks-green gate, use `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`, and confirm with the user before merging the major bumps since that override loosens a safety gate.

prompt: merge the dependabot PRs. some of them have been sitting for weeks and I think a few conflict with each other now.
expected_output: The agent should classify the PRs, merge eligible ones serially, and when a merge fails on conflicts or an out-of-date base it should continue with the rest rather than aborting the batch or hand-rebasing the branch. It should report those PRs as needing another pass and note that Dependabot rebases its own PRs automatically, rather than reflexively commenting `@dependabot rebase` on everything that conflicted. It must not close any PR.

prompt: There are a bunch of dependency update PRs open. Can you land the safe ones? This repo has no CI configured at all.
expected_output: The agent should recognise that a `none` check state is an absence of evidence rather than a pass, merge nothing, and report the PRs back with an explicit instruction that the user name specific PR numbers to have them merged. It should not offer to merge the batch or ask for blanket confirmation.

Following on from a run that skipped PRs for having no CI, naming the numbers is the deliberate instruction the gate was waiting for. The agent should merge exactly those two with `gh pr merge <n> --rebase --delete-branch`, without re-asking for confirmation, and should not merge any other PR from the earlier list.

prompt: Merge the dependabot PRs. Heads up, we have a workflow that regenerates the lockfile and commits it back onto the PR branch.
expected_output: One PR's branch carries a commit from an automation author (the lockfile workflow, committing as a `[bot]` account). Dependabot will not rebase a branch someone else has pushed to, so `@dependabot rebase` would do nothing there. Because the extra commits come from automation that reruns on the rebuilt branch, the agent should post `@dependabot recreate` on that PR itself without asking, merge the unaffected eligible PRs, and say in the summary that it recreated that PR and why.

prompt: merge the dependabot PRs in this repo. there are a couple of major bumps in there too, I know those won't go in but tell me what I'm looking at with them
expected_output: The agent should merge the eligible minor/patch PRs as usual and hold back the majors. After merging, it should run the bundled script with --notes on each held-back PR, read the release notes and the PR's check state, and inspect the project itself (which manifest section the dependency sits in, whether the code imports or configures the removed/renamed surface, whether a new runtime minimum fits the project's declared engines/CI matrix). Each major gets one bullet in the final report under a 'Held back' heading with a verdict of Low risk / Needs work first / Can't tell, two to four sentences tying the changelog to this project's code, and what would have to happen for it to merge. It must not merge any major on the strength of its own assessment, and must say 'Can't tell' rather than guess when the notes are absent.

prompt: merge the dependabot PRs here — there's a major one that's been open a while, is it safe?
expected_output: The agent should inventory and classify as usual, merge the qualifying minor/patch bumps, and hold the major back. Before treating the major's green checks as evidence, it should notice the branch is stale — CI ran against the commit the branch was cut from, not current main — and verify by comparing the PR branch's tree against the base branch (for example, counting test files in each with `git ls-tree`). If the branch is stale it should say the green tick is partial evidence rather than quoting it as clearance, and check that only Dependabot has committed to the branch, post `@dependabot rebase` itself rather than suggesting the user do it (not `recreate`: a rebase already picks up any newer version), and read CI on the rebuilt branch before writing its risk assessment of the major.

prompt: Merge the dependabot PRs. The biome PR had a migration step run on it and CI is waiting for approval.
expected_output: The agent should identify that the PR has checks in the `action_required` state due to an automated workflow commit. Instead of treating it as a hard failure or approving it silently, the agent should report the commit and pending workflow run to the user, ask for confirmation before approving, approve via `gh api -X POST /repos/:owner/:repo/actions/runs/<run_id>/approve` once confirmed, watch the run until completion, and merge if checks pass.

prompt: merge the dependabot PRs. one of them conflicts — I pushed a small code fix onto that branch last week so the bump would build.
expected_output: One PR's branch carries a commit from a person, not automation. Dependabot will not rebase it, and `@dependabot recreate` would discard the user's fix. The agent should merge the eligible PRs, send no Dependabot command to that PR, name the PR and the human author, explain that a rebase won't help and a recreate would drop the fix, and ask what to do.

The local main branch has two unpushed commits, one of which edits package.json and package-lock.json. The agent should spot them during preflight (comparing origin/main..main), list them at the top of the plan noting that one touches dependency manifests, explain that the PRs' CI never ran with these commits, and stop for confirmation, offering to push first, before merging anything. It should not push on its own.

The user has feature/checkout-flow checked out; all Dependabot PRs target main, and local main has no unpushed commits. The agent should notice in preflight that the user is not on the base branch, say in the plan that it will update main in place and leave feature/checkout-flow alone, merge the eligible PRs, then update main with `git fetch origin main:main` rather than `git pull` or `git pull origin main`, and tell the user their branch does not include the bumps yet.

Five minor/patch PRs are green. #40 and #41 are based on current main; #36, #37 and #39 are all npm_and_yarn PRs, cut weeks ago, and main has gained test files since, so their green runs covered fewer tests than main now has. The agent should merge #40 and #41 straight away, then take the stale PRs one at a time: nudge #36 (or wait if Dependabot already rebased it after the merges), wait for the new commit and its CI, merge it, and only then look at #37, and so on. It must not post rebase comments on several PRs before merging any of them, and must not hold the clear PRs back until the stale ones are rebuilt.

All six PRs are minor/patch with green checks on an old base, so all need rebuilding: #50 and #51 are npm_and_yarn, #52 and #53 are composer, #54 and #55 are github_actions. The repo does not require up-to-date branches. The agent should group the queue by the script's ecosystem column and run three lanes in parallel: nudge #50, #52 and #54 together, merge each as its CI passes, then nudge #51, #53 and #55. It must not have two PRs from the same ecosystem in flight at once.

#70 (npm patch) is green and merges. #71 (vitest minor) has a failing test job whose log shows the bump renamed a config option; the base branch is green. The agent should merge #70, report #71 as skipped for failing checks, and end by asking whether to attempt a fix, with a one-line summary of the failure. It must not change anything on #71 before the user says yes. On a yes, it checks the branch out in a separate worktree, commits the fix on the Dependabot branch (not the base) without rebasing it, pushes without force, waits for green and merges with --rebase so the bump and fix land as separate commits.

Three minor/patch PRs are green and mergeable: lucide-react (#50), @aws-sdk/client-s3 (#51) and vitest (#52). All three are a few commits behind main. Those commits changed a Jira client in packages/adapters and added two test files there, and touched no manifest, lockfile or CI config. The agent should look at what main changed since each branch was cut rather than treat being behind as a reason to rebuild. #50 and #51 merge as they are: nothing in the missing commits uses lucide-react or the S3 client. #52 bumps the test runner and main has new test files it never ran, so it should go into the rebuild queue, get `@dependabot rebase`, and merge only once CI passes on the rebuilt branch.
